findings.title: Denial cache never invalidated on permission grants, can cause stale denies
findings.body: The denial cache entry (permDenialCache) is set with shortCacheTTL but there is no invalidation when a user's permissions change (e.g. after being granted access to a resource). Although TTL is short (30s), during that window a user who was just granted access to a resource they were previously denied will continue to be denied, which directly works against the stated goal of this PR (allowing users to access resources they just created/were granted). Since permission grants aren't necessarily reflected until the next TTL expiry, this cache can mask legitimate permission updates for up to 30s with no proactive invalidation path.

findings.title: Cached permission check short-circuits only when allowed=true, hiding stale denies from cache but not reducing DB calls on deny
findings.body: In Check(), when getCachedIdentityPermissions succeeds but checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through and re-fetches permissions from the DB and performs the full check again. This means cache hits for a user who lacks the permission always double the work (cached check + DB fetch + check again) instead of simply trusting the fresh DB fetch result, which could be returned directly from the second check without doing both. This is a performance regression for all 'denied' or missing permission cases, somewhat defeating the purpose of the permission cache for negative outcomes aside from the explicit denial cache for exact name/folder lookups since the denial cache key depends on exact Name/ParentFolder which won't match for other requested names and thus won't prevent repeated DB round trips for the same user+action+different resource names that are also denied.

findings.title: Metric mislabeling: permissionCacheUsage recorded 'false' even on cache hit when permission denied
findings.body: When the cached permission check at line 123 returns allowed=false (cache hit occurred but resource not allowed), the code proceeds to line 137 and records permissionCacheUsage with 'false', incorrectly implying there was no cache hit. This produces misleading metrics about actual cache utilization, since a cache hit did occur yet is counted as a miss when the cached result happened to be a denial for this specific resource.
